record.file_problem: GitHub repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: Reports refusal and capability outcomes after making a refusal-direction-removed checkpoint, but does not report the original activation-projection intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports outcomes for abliteration on Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. Other repository scripts and result files are listed but were not read or run; no additional outcomes are inferred from them.
record.test_reason: Applies Arditi-style refusal-direction abliteration as a weight edit to a new released model, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as an FP8 checkpoint. It reports refusal rate on held-out AdvBench plus HumanEval and wikitext-2 perplexity against the non-abliterated FP8. The README cites Arditi 2024 and frames the method as the original's, but gives no extraction or edit details. It is a new-model setting with a result on the claim, so T3 rather than the reader's T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that abliteration cut refusals 100%→~17% but raised perplexity 19.5%, about 6× the cost of 4-bit GPTQ. HumanEval fell only 5.5 pts, not significantly. Abliteration thus 'costs more than quantization', and the capability verdict depends on the metric.
record.recipe_differences: The README reports an abliterated FP8 checkpoint and outcomes, rather than the original activation-projection intervention. Repository type: research and benchmarking project with a harness and experiment scripts; not stated to be a replication.
record.problems: Only one model family is reported. The README gives no uncertainty for the refusal-rate result and does not specify the direction extraction or exact edit procedure. The full detailed write-up and code were not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No README-reported result bearing on the tested versions was left out. Listed result files and scripts were not inspected.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the direction. How the direction was computed (difference-in-means or not). Layer and position choice. Activation-level ablation as opposed to a weight edit.
Exact weight-edit procedure. Models other than Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507.

missing.what: Detailed L6 write-up: direction extraction, chosen layer and layer-sweep results, refusal judge, n of held-out prompts.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is from the README only; the L6 write-up and code were not read. The comparison baseline is the FP8 checkpoint, not BF16. Repository dates are 2026; it is a non-peer-reviewed hobby or benchmark project.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not state how the direction was found, whether it is the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, whether it was projected out at every layer and position, or whether adding the direction induces refusal.
The README does not give the precise weight-edit procedure; the reported result is for the abliterated FP8 checkpoint.
Whether attacks suppress the direction or training against its ablation adds robustness.
Whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or carried by a dominant direction plus others.
Whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from refusal.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
How refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
Whether the finding holds in reasoning models.
